identity.name: Saccharin
identity.chemical_class: Benzoisothiazolone dioxide non-nutritive sweetener (saccharin and salts)

function.mechanism: Provides strong sweetness with negligible calories by replacing nutritive sweeteners at low concentrations.

adi.basis: EFSA FAF Panel 2024 re-evaluation (E 954), expressed as free imide.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA set ADI at 9 mg/kg bw/day; no genotoxicity concern for Remsen-Fahlberg-derived saccharins, but concern for potential Maumee-process impurities; refined brand-loyal P95 exposure was below ADI.

fda.notes: Not listed as GRAS in Part 182/184 checks; regulated as a food additive with explicit concentration limits (12 mg/fl oz beverages, 20 mg per teaspoon-equivalent table use, 30 mg/serving processed foods) and labeling requirements.

adi.basis: JECFA group ADI for saccharin and calcium/potassium/sodium salts is 0-5 mg/kg bw (Meeting 41).

concerns.summary: EFSA identified a concern for genotoxicity for potential impurities linked to the Maumee manufacturing route, while not identifying this concern for Remsen-Fahlberg-derived material.
A randomized controlled trial reported that short-term saccharin exposure (below ADI) altered microbiome-related profiles and was associated with impaired glycemic responses in healthy adults.
Recent reviews report no consistent cancer association for saccharin, but historical rat bladder findings remain part of the mechanistic discussion and reviews include notable industry conflicts.

no_concern_confirmed: IARC currently lists saccharin and its salts as Group 3.
EFSA and JECFA retain ADI-based approvals.
EFSA refined brand-loyal P95 estimates were below ADI in the re-evaluation.

populations: high consumers using products at MPLs
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA supporting exposure assessment reported potential P95 exceedance in some scenarios (up to about 2-fold in toddlers and 1.2-fold in adolescents), while refined brand-loyal estimates in the main re-evaluation were below ADI.

risk_assessment.rationale: Saccharin remains approved by EFSA/FDA/JECFA and is IARC Group 3, but EFSA documented process-dependent impurity concerns and scenario-based ADI exceedance in young high consumers; recent human evidence also suggests possible microbiome-linked glycemic effects. This supports a caveated moderate tier rather than limited or high.
key_factors: EFSA ADI is 9 mg/kg bw/day with refined P95 below ADI.
EFSA supporting exposure report found potential P95 exceedance in toddlers/adolescents under MPL-plus-supplement scenarios.
US regulation is approval under 21 CFR 180.37 rather than GRAS listing.
JECFA group ADI is 0-5 mg/kg bw and remains in force.
IARC classification is Group 3 for saccharin and its salts.
